claim: Brahmanical and Saiva religious presence in ancient and early-medieval Sri Lanka coexisted with Buddhist political and monastic institutions rather than being reducible to the later Kandyan pattern in which Hindu deities were ritually subordinated within a Buddhist ceremonial hierarchy.
bounded_by: The claim establishes analytically distinct coexistence mechanisms; it does not quantify Hindu adherence in the Anuradhapura population or assert continuous royal patronage of every shrine mentioned by the museum.
notes: Explicit anti-collapse rule: do not label both Anuradhapura coexistence and Kandy Perahera incorporation simply as 'syncretism'.
